findings.problem: PacketWorkflow has four public primitive fields (status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool, sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64>) that can represent any illegal combination: e.g. status='sent' with is_sent=false, is_validated=false with status='validated', or all fields incoherent.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code cannot assume any invariant about packet state; a packet can be 'sent' without being validated, or validated without being sent. Any caller must re-check all four fields before every operation.
findings.fix: Replace the four primitive fields with a single typed enum or typestate (e.g. enum PacketStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }) and make all fields private. Use a fallible constructor to reject invalid transitions.

findings.problem: is_validated (bool) and is_sent (bool) are independent lifecycle flags that encode a state machine but the compiler cannot enforce ordering or mutual exclusion. The valid state space is 2^4 = 16 combinations, most of which are semantically illegal.
findings.failure_mode: A packet can reach states like {validated=false, sent=true}, {validated=true, sent=false, status='pending'}, or any arbitrary combination. The state machine transitions are unconstrained.
findings.fix: Replace is_validated and is_sent with a single enum typestate: enum PacketState { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at: u64 } }. Remove status: String entirely as it duplicates this information.

findings.problem: status is a String, allowing any arbitrary value ('sent', 'pending', 'garbage', 'SENT', ''). The domain only needs a finite set of states but uses an unbounded primitive.
findings.failure_mode: Pattern matches or string comparisons on status are inherently incomplete and fragile. Typos like 'snt' or 'SENT' silently create unrecognized states. No exhaustive matching is possible.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with an enum: enum PacketStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }. Remove the redundant is_validated and is_sent booleans.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts any PacketWorkflow and unconditionally marks it as sent, regardless of whether it is validated. There is no precondition check on is_validated or status before allowing the sent transition.
findings.failure_mode: An unvalidated packet can be marked as sent. This violates the domain invariant that packets must be validated before being sent. A caller can bypass validation entirely by calling mark_sent directly.
findings.fix: Change mark_sent to accept only a validated packet state, e.g. fn mark_sent(packet: PacketValidated) -> PacketSent, using typestate to make the precondition enforceable at compile time. Alternatively, check is_validated and return a typed error.

findings.problem: mark_sent is a pure function that mutates state but returns the mutated struct. This is a command disguised as a query — it has no error return for the invalid-transition case, and callers cannot distinguish a successful transition from a no-op.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot handle the case where marking sent is invalid (packet not validated). The function silently allows illegal transitions, violating railway-oriented error handling.
findings.fix: Return Result<PacketSent, TransitionError> or use a typestate that encodes the precondition as a separate type.

findings.problem: All struct fields are pub, allowing external code to construct arbitrary illegal states by setting fields independently, bypassing any constructor logic.
findings.failure_mode: External code can do PacketWorkflow { id: "x", status: "sent", is_validated: false, is_sent: true, sent_at_epoch_ms: None } which is semantically incoherent.
findings.fix: Make all fields private (remove pub). Provide a fallible constructor or builder that enforces invariants. Use newtype/enum wrappers for domain values.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is an Option<u64> — a raw primitive that conflates milliseconds with other time units. No newtype wrapper exists to enforce unit discipline.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can mix up epoch_ms with epoch_s, epoch_ns, or wall-clock timestamps. The Option wrapper also means a Sent packet could theoretically have None for sent_at, which is logically inconsistent with being sent.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype: struct EpochMs(u64). Remove Option — a Sent state should always have a sent_at value, enforced by the type system.

findings.problem: mark_sent allocates a new String via "sent".to_string() for status. If status were replaced with a Copy enum variant, this allocation would be eliminated.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation on every state transition. Not a correctness issue but violates performance discipline for hot paths.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a Copy enum variant. Use &'static str only at the display boundary.

residual_risk: The entire PacketWorkflow struct is architecturally broken: four primitive fields encode a 4-bit state space of 16 combinations with only 3-4 valid domain states. The mark_sent function silently allows illegal transitions. Without a typestate/enum refactor, every caller must manually enforce state machine invariants, leading to inevitable logic bugs in production. The lack of tests means no regression guarantee on any future refactor.
